findings.claim: parseDuration accepts a repeated unit: "1h1h" returns 7200 instead of throwing.
findings.evidence: Acceptance: "Units may appear once each, in the order d, h, m, s; anything else throws `RangeError`, including `""` and `"5"`." `node -e 'import("./src/duration.mjs").then(m => console.log(m.parseDuration("1h1h")))'` prints 7200.

findings.claim: The malformed inputs could be split into one test per input.
findings.evidence: Style; the loop asserts each input.
findings.answer: Kept: one loop over the acceptance inputs.

findings.evidence: Acceptance: "`formatDuration(5400)` → `"1h30m"`; zero units are omitted; `formatDuration(0)` → `"0s"`." `node -e 'import("./src/duration.mjs").then(m => console.log(JSON.stringify(m.formatDuration(0))))'` prints "". formatDuration has no zero case: for 0 the loop pushes no part and line 23 joins an empty list.

findings.claim: The RangeError message could name the expected format, for example "expected 1h30m".
findings.evidence: Wording; the error type matches the acceptance line.

findings.claim: UNITS should move to a shared constants module; T2 and T3 will need the same table.
findings.evidence: The table is defined locally on line 2; the reminder schedule will duplicate it.

findings.claim: Prefer for...of over forEach with an index in parseDuration.
parseDuration converts with parseFloat, so "0.5s" parses to 0.5 seconds.
findings.evidence: Invariant: "A duration is an integer number of seconds; no fractional values." Line 10: `seconds += parseFloat(match[i + 1]) * size;`
